output.title: Branch office to data centre
output.description: A branch and internet customers reach a data centre through edge routers, an active-standby firewall pair, a spine and leaf fabric and a load balancer pair. The firewall's rules allow web traffic and deny the branch any path to the payments zone.

simulations.title: One firewall fails over
simulations.description: The active firewall dies mid-traffic. The standby takes over in a few seconds: requests wait at the pair, none are lost.

action.text: Customers come in over the internet and the branch over SD-WAN. Both pass the firewall pair: one unit carries the traffic, the other stands by.
The active firewall fails. For a few seconds, while the standby notices and takes over its sessions, requests wait at the pair.
The standby carries everything now, at the same throughput: nothing was dropped. Until the failed unit is back, though, the pair has no spare.

expectations.label: Requests wait while it fails over
The firewall never drops a request

simulations.title: The firewall blocks the branch from payments
simulations.description: Someone at the branch tries Payments' admin API. The firewall's deny rule stops every request: blocked on purpose, not lost.

action.text: The branch reaches the shop's back office through the firewall. Its rules allow web traffic, and deny the branch any path to Payments, which sits in the PCI zone.
Someone at the branch starts calling Payments' admin API.
Every one of those requests stops at the firewall: the deny rule blocks it. Blocked isn't lost; it's the rule working.

expectations.label: The firewall blocks the admin requests
Nothing is dropped at the firewall
